newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Time to float Telecom unit in mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Time to float Telecom unit in mid-1997.

text.p: Malaysia's Time Engineering Bhd said on Monday it will offer a "sizeable" number of shares in the initial public offering (IPO) of its telecommunications subsidiary in the middle of this year.

The offering for newly set-up Time Telecommunications Holdings Bhd will include an offer of convertible loan stocks and a telephone package for its cellular services, company officials told a news conference.
Time will transfer its fixed line network, cellular phone company Sapura Digital Sdn Bhd and pay-phone operator Uniphone Sdn Bhd to Time Telecom for the flotation.
Time officials said the company will remain the majority shareholder in the listed entity.

They said Time Telecom will be floated under the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange guidelines for infrastructure project companies which allow for the listing of companies without a track record. The officials said they could not give much details of the IPO until they received a listing approval from the Securities Commission.
Time Telecom chief operating officer Donald James Rae said the IPO will only be offered to local investors.
Most of the proceeds will be used to improve its cellular phone services which currently has 90,000 subscribers, he said.
On the loan stocks and telephone package, Time Engineering chairman Shamsir Omar said the company wants to achieve a different form of relationship between a customer and his telephone company.
"When you make a call, you are generating income or profit for us and for you," he said.
The telephone package will include a free cellular phone, low monthly access fee and competitive airtime tariff.

Asked about equal access for the local telecommunications industry, Rae said an earlier starting date would be beneficial for the company but its strategy will be for the deregulation to start as scheduled on January 1, 1999.
"Our planning horizon says January 1, 1999," Rae said. "If it moves forward, it's very beneficial for us."

Time has said previously that it was negotiating with the government to have equal access for long distance and international calls to start earlier, but the proposal is being resisted by Telekom Malaysia Bhd.
